Let me look at the language carefully.

We have:
- labels Low, High
- flows_to: High -> Low is False, else True
- join: Low,Low=Low; else High
- security records: reader, indirect_reader
- wf_security kappa := flows_to kappa.indirect_reader kappa.reader (i.e., indirect reader must flow to reader)
- security_le kappa1 kappa2 := flows_to k1.reader k2.reader /\ flows_to k1.indirect_reader k2.indirect_reader

ty_protect l T applies protect_security to the top-level security.

wf_ty: recursively wf.

Adequacy: R T_result (plug C t1) (plug C t2) → same_result. Since ir T_result = Low (from the hypothesis), R unfolds to: forall v1 v2, evaluates → V T_result v1 v2. V strong (ir T_result Low) gives structural equality: by induction on T_result (ground, transparent):

Fixpoint R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\ security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists a1 b1 k1 a2 b2 k2,
          v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2 /\ R T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->

  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>

Then subst_fvar:
Fixpoint subst_fvar (sigma : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => sigma x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_fvar sigma body) k
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_fvar sigma t1) (subst_fvar sigma t2) r
  | tm_pair t1 t2 k => tm_pair (subst_fvar sigma t1) (subst_fvar sigma t2) k
  | tm_fst t1 r => tm_fst (subst_fvar sigma t1) r
  | tm_snd t1 r => tm_snd (subst_fvar sigma t1) r
  | tm_inl t1 k => tm_inl (subst_fvar sigma t1) k
  | tm_inr t1 k => tm_inr (subst_fvar sigma t1) k
  | tm_case t0 b1 b2 r => tm_case (subst_fvar sigma t0) (subst_fvar sigma b1) (subst_fvar sigma b2) r
  | tm_protect l t1 => tm_protect l (subst_fvar sigma t1)
  | tm_if c y n r => tm_if (subst_fvar sigma c) (subst_fvar sigma y) (subst_fvar sigma n) r
  end.

Definition extend (x : atom) (u : tm) (sigma : atom -> tm) : atom -> tm :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb x y then u else sigma y.

Fixpoint R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  flows_to (security_of T).(indirect_reader) Low ->
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
    match T with

        exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\
                      security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k
    | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
        (exists a1 k1 a2 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2) \/
        (exists b1 k1 b2 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T2 b1 b2)
    | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
        exists a1 b1 k1 a2 b2 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2 /\ R T2 b1 b2

    end.
```

Prove step_deterministic by induction on the first step derivation with case analysis on the second:

Lemma step_det : forall t u1, step t u1 -> forall u2, step t u2 -> u1 = u2.
Proof.
  intros t u1 H. induction H; intros u2 H2; inversion H2; subst; try reflexivity;
  (* recursive cases: use IH *)
  ...
Let me enumerate the step constructors and their cases:
1. ST_AppAbs: t = app (abs T body k) v r, u1 = protect k.ir (open body v), premises value (abs), value v, flows.
   H2 : step (app (abs...) v r) u2. Inversion gives:
   - ST_AppAbs: u2 = protect k.ir (open body v) (same) → reflexivity ✓.
   - ST_App1: premise step (abs...) t1' → impossible.
   - ST_App2: premise value (abs), step v t2' → contradicts value v.
2. ST_App1: t = app t1 t2 r, t1 --> t1', u1 = app t1' t2 r, IH : forall u2, t1 --> u2 -> t1' = u2.
   H2 cases: ST_AppAbs (t1 = abs... but then step (abs) t1' contradicts); ST_App1: u2 = app t1'' t2 r with t1 --> t1'' → IH gives t1' = t1'' → subst → refl; ST_App2: premise value t1 and t1 --> t1' → value_no_step contradiction.
3. ST_App2: t = app v1 t2 r with value v1, t2 --> t2', u1 = app v1 t2' r, IH about t2 --> ...
   H2: ST_AppAbs: v1 = abs and value t2 and flows → u2 = protect ...; but t2 --> t2' and value t2 contradict.
       ST_App1: premise step v1 t1' → value_no_step contradiction.
       ST_App2: u2 = app v1 t2'' r with t2 --> t2'' → IH → refl.
4. ST_Pair1: u1 = pair t1' t2 k, IH about t1 --> ...
   H2: ST_Pair1 → IH; ST_Pair2 with premise value t1 and t1 --> t1' → contradiction.
5. ST_Pair2: symmetric.
6. ST_FstPair: t = fst (pair v1 v2 k) r, u1 = protect k.ir v1, premises values, flows.
   H2: ST_FstPair → same ✓; ST_Fst with premise step (pair v1 v2 k) t' → value_no_step contradiction (pair is a value).
7. ST_Fst: u1 = fst t' r, IH about t --> t'.
   H2: ST_FstPair: t = pair v1 v2 k with values → contradicts step t t' (value_no_step); ST_Fst: IH → refl.
8. ST_SndPair, ST_Snd: symmetric.
9. ST_Inl: u1 = inl t' k, IH about t --> t'.
   H2: ST_Inl: IH → refl. (Only one rule for inl.) Actually ST_Inl is the only rule with tm_inl on the left ✓.
10. ST_Inr: same.
11. ST_CaseLeft: t = case (inl v k) b1 b2 r, u1 = protect k.ir (open b1 v), premises value v, flows.
    H2: ST_CaseLeft → same (k'? the value is inl v k, so matching gives the same k) ✓ refl; ST_CaseRight: the scrutinee is inl vs inr → impossible; ST_Case: premise step (inl v k) t' → value_no_step ✓.
12. ST_CaseRight: symmetric.
13. ST_Case: u1 = case t' b1 b2 r, IH.
    H2: ST_CaseLeft: t = inl v k with value v → contradicts step t t'; ST_CaseRight similarly; ST_Case: IH → refl.
14. ST_ProtectValue: t = protect l v, value v, u1 = protect_value v l.
    H2: ST_ProtectValue: same ✓; ST_Protect: premise step v t' → value_no_step ✓.
15. ST_Protect: u1 = protect l t', IH.
    H2: ST_ProtectValue: t = value and step t t' → contradiction; ST_Protect: IH → refl.
16. ST_If: u1 = if c' y n r, IH.
    H2: ST_If: IH; ST_IfTrue/False: c = inl/inr with value → contradicts step.
17. ST_IfTrue: t = if (inl v k) y n r, u1 = protect k.ir y, premises value v, flows.
    H2: ST_If → premise step (inl v k) c' → contradiction; ST_IfTrue → same; ST_IfFalse → inl vs inr contradiction.
18. ST_IfFalse: symmetric.

So the proof is a big case analysis. A uniform tactic could handle it: after `induction H; intros u2 H2; inversion H2; subst`, the remaining goals are:
(a) reflexivity goals (same rule) ✓ try reflexivity.
(b) contradictions from value_no_step (hypotheses value X and step X Y) — handle with match.
(c) contradictions from step_abs (step (abs) X) — handle with step_abs_false.
(d) recursive same-rule cases needing the IH: e.g., ST_App1 vs ST_App1: goal app t1' t2 r = app t1'' t2 r, with IH : forall u2, t1 --> u2 -> t1' = u2 and H : t1 --> t1''. Match-based: `match goal with IH : forall u, ?x --> u -> ?y = u, H : ?x --> ?z |- ?y = ?z => exact (IH z H) end`.
(e) constructor-mismatch contradictions (inl vs inr): inversion should give an impossible equation like tm_inl = tm_inr; `discriminate` handles.

Let me write the tactic:
  intros t u1 H. induction H; intros u2 H2; inversion H2; subst;
    try reflexivity;
    try discriminate;
    try (exfalso; match goal with
         | Hs : tm_abs _ _ _ --> _ |- _ => exact (step_abs_false _ _ _ _ Hs)
         | Hs : _ --> _, Hv : value ?x |- _ => exact (value_no_step x Hv _ Hs)
         end);
    try (match goal with
         | IH : forall u, ?x --> u -> ?y = u, Hs : ?x --> ?z |- ?y = ?z => exact (IH z Hs)
         end).

- Arrow: goal R (Arrow T1 T2 k) t1 t2 = guard -> forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> exists abs shapes ...; apply HR with the evaluations of t1',t2' derived via the determinism lemma ✓; HR gives the abs shapes and the clause about v1,v2 ✓. Fixpoint R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      flows_to k.ir Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\ security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.ir Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        (exists a1 k1 a2 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\ security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2) \/

  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k => ... 
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.ir Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->

Definition details:

Fixpoint R (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2 /\
                      security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        (exists a1 k1 a2 k2, v1 = tm_inl a1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl a2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2) \/
        (exists b1 k1 b2 k2, v1 = tm_inr b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr b2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T2 b1 b2)
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists a1 b1 k1 a2 b2 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\
          security_le k1 k /\ security_le k2 k /\ R T1 a1 a2 /\ R T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 k =>
      flows_to k.(indirect_reader) Low ->
      forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 ->
        exists T1' body1 k1 T2' body2 k2,
          v1 = tm_abs T1' body1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_abs T2' body2 k2 /\

          (forall u1 u2 r, flows_to k.(reader) r -> R T1 u1 u2 ->
             R T2 (tm_app v1 u1 r) (tm_app v2 u2 r))
  end.

Line 1411 is in lookup_cons_other: `rewrite Nat.eqb_neq; [reflexivity | exact H].` — Nat.eqb_neq : forall n m, (n =? m) = false <-> n <> m. `rewrite Nat.eqb_neq` tries to rewrite using the iff; the goal after simpl is `(if x =? y then Some T else lookup_context x Gamma) = lookup_context x Gamma`. Rewriting with Nat.eqb_neq needs to find an occurrence of `(x =? y) = false`, i.e., the occurrence of Nat.eqb x y as a subterm of the if-condition. The `rewrite Nat.eqb_neq` with an iff whose LHS is `(?n =? ?m) = false` should rewrite occurrences of `(x =? y)` to false if it can instantiate. The error says no subterm matching `(?n =? ?n0) = false` — because the goal has `Nat.eqb x y` as a *proposition in the if*, not as an equality `= false`. Hmm, the if's condition is `Nat.eqb x y : bool`; to rewrite it via Nat.eqb_neq I need the lemma stated as an equality of booleans: `Nat.eqb_neq x y : (x =? y) = false <-> x <> y`. Rewriting a boolean subterm with an iff is not directly possible (rewrite works on Props, and (x =? y) = false is a Prop; the if-condition is the boolean term, not the Prop).

Better: use `apply Nat.eqb_neq` to get the boolean equality, then rewrite:
  assert (E : (x =? y) = false) by (apply Nat.eqb_neq; exact H).
  rewrite E. reflexivity.

Let me write the decomposition lemma first:

Lemma multi_app_gen : forall t w, multi t w ->
  forall f a r, t = tm_app f a r -> value w ->
  exists vf va T1' body k, value vf /\ multi f vf /\ value va /\ multi a va /\
    vf = tm_abs T1' body k /\ flows_to k.(reader) r /\
    multi (tm_protect k.(indirect_reader) (open body va)) w.
Proof.
  intros t w Hm. induction Hm as [| t1 t2 t3 Hs Hm IH]; intros f a r Heq Hw.
  - subst t1. inversion Hw.
  - subst t1. inversion Hs; subst.
    + (* ST_AppAbs *) exists (tm_abs T body kappa), v, T, body, kappa. repeat split; auto; constructor.
    + (* ST_App1 *) destruct (IH f' a r eq_refl Hw) as [...]; exists ...; multi f vf via multi_step ✓.
    + (* ST_App2 *) destruct (IH f a' r eq_refl Hw) ...; multi a va via multi_step ✓.
Qed.

The constructor order for app: ST_AppAbs, ST_App1, ST_App2 ✓.

Then evaluates_app_decomp:
Lemma evaluates_app_decomp : forall f a r w, evaluates (tm_app f a r) w ->
  exists vf va T1' body k, value vf /\ evaluates f vf /\ value va /\ evaluates a va /\
    vf = tm_abs T1' body k /\ flows_to k.(reader) r /\
    evaluates (tm_protect k.(indirect_reader) (open body va)) w.
✓ directly from multi_app_gen with the equation refl.

multi_app_abs_step:
Lemma multi_app_abs_step : forall T1 body k u r v,
  value (tm_abs T1 body k) -> multi u v -> value v -> flows_to k.(reader) r ->
  multi (tm_app (tm_abs T1 body k) u r) (tm_protect k.(indirect_reader) (open body v)).
Proof.
  intros T1 body k u r v Hvabs Hm Hval Hfl. induction Hm as [| a b c Hs Hm IH].
  - (* multi_refl: u = v *) subst a. econstructor; [apply ST_AppAbs; [exact Hvabs | exact Hval | exact Hfl] | constructor].
  - (* step *) econstructor; [apply ST_App2; [exact Hvabs | exact Hs] | apply IH; exact Hval].
Qed.

Lemma R_app_aux : forall T2 T1 kappa f1 f2 a1 a2 r,
  R (Ty_Arrow T1 T2 kappa) f1 f2 ->

  R T1 a1 a2 ->
  R T2 (tm_app f1 a1 r) (tm_app f2 a2 r).

  all: intros Hflow w1 w2 E1 E2.
  all: destruct (evaluates_app_decomp f1 a1 r w1 E1) as
